entities.summary: William Frederick Schelter was a professor of mathematics at The University of Texas at Austin and a Lisp developer and programmer. Schelter is credited with the development of the GNU Common Lisp (GCL) implementation of Common Lisp and the GPL'd version of the computer algebra system Macsyma called Maxima. Schelter authored Austin Kyoto Common Lisp (AKCL) under contract with IBM. AKCL formed the foundation for Axiom, another computer algebra system. AKCL eventually became GNU Common Lisp. He is also credited with the first port of the GNU C compiler to the Intel 386 architecture, used in the original implementation of the Linux kernel.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Schelter's work on GNU Common Lisp and Maxima enabled significant advancements in computer algebra systems, contributing to the development of Axiom and influencing the creation of the Linux kernel. His porting of the GNU C compiler to Intel 386 architecture had a lasting impact on the open-source software community.
